description: Checks a price someone has claimed for a product against the prices WEM has itself observed at retailers (recent readings, within a small tolerance; not a live quote), and reports the cheapest observed offer. Identify the product by gtin (strongest), slug, wem_id, provider + externalId, or title (weakest, relevance-checked). `retailer` names the shop the claim is about; without it the nearest observed price at any shop is checked. Only offers in the claim's currency are compared. Verdicts: confirmed (WEM observed that price there), price_moved (WEM last observed a different price there), not_at_retailer (WEM has no observed price there, though it may hold a feed price), no_claim (no price given; the offers are returned), unknown_product (the product could not be resolved, or WEM holds no observed price for it in that currency). unknown_product means the claim could not be checked, not that it is false. `lastConfirmedAt` says when WEM last observed a price in the answer, or is null. Each call records an evidence receipt, whose id can be cited later.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for the claimed price. Default GBP. Only offers in this currency are compared.

externalId.description: That listing's own id (ASIN, eBay item number). Use with provider.

gtin.description: Product barcode: EAN-13, UPC-A, EAN-8 or GTIN-14. Strongest identifier.

price.description: The price being claimed. Omit to ask only for the observed offers.

provider.description: With externalId: the retailer source of a listing that identifies the product, e.g. 'amazon' or 'ebay'. To name the shop the claim is about, use `retailer`.

retailer.description: The shop the price was claimed at, as a slug or display name. Omit to compare against every shop.

slug.description: WEM canonical slug, as in wem3.ai/pl/{slug}.

title.description: Product title. The weakest identifier: used only when no id is given, and only if it passes a relevance check.

wem_id.description: WEM ID (W + 10 Crockford characters + check). Active catalogue products only.

name: verify_offer

outputSchema.description: `unknown_product` means the claim could NOT be checked. It never means the claim is false and must not be reported as one.

betterBy.description: Saving from taking `cheapest` over the claimed price. Never negative.

affiliate.description: False when this link earns WEM nothing: the shop has no affiliate programme with WEM, or this link does not carry one. It is still a real offer, and its link is not affiliate-tracked. Absent (or true) means the link is affiliate-tracked. `disclosure` states whether all, some or none of the links are tracked.

inStock.description: null means the retailer did not report availability. Say "stock not confirmed" — never present null as in stock.

totalCost.description: Item plus any stated extras. When unknown is non-empty, delivered is a floor — never relay it as what the shopper will pay.

affiliate.description: False when this link earns WEM nothing: the shop has no affiliate programme with WEM, or this link does not carry one. It is still a real offer, and its link is not affiliate-tracked. Absent (or true) means the link is affiliate-tracked. `disclosure` states whether all, some or none of the links are tracked.

inStock.description: null means the retailer did not report availability. Say "stock not confirmed" — never present null as in stock.

totalCost.description: Item plus any stated extras. When unknown is non-empty, delivered is a floor — never relay it as what the shopper will pay.

comparisonSet.description: How wide the comparison behind `cheapest` was. `exhaustive` is always false: WEM does not see every retailer, so `cheapest` is the lowest offer WEM holds, never the lowest that exists. Relay it as such.

exhaustive.description: Always false. Never present this answer as the lowest price available anywhere.

disclosure.description: WEM’s affiliate disclosure for this answer, written to be quoted as it is. Its wording changes with the rows: it states whether every outbound link is affiliate-tracked, only some are, or none are. A version from an earlier answer may not fit this one: a row marked `affiliate: false` earns WEM nothing.

identity.description: How the product was identified — a separate question from whether the price checks out. Never present a `strength` of "inferred" as a verified identity.

strength.description: exact = barcode; catalogued = a WEM key or the retailer’s own listing id; inferred = matched on the product name and still a guess.

lastConfirmedAt.description: When WEM last read a price among the offers compared — the freshness of this answer. Null means none of them carries a dated reading: say the prices are undated.

offers.description: Prices WEM holds for this product, including indicative ones and shops it has no affiliate programme with yet. When `cheapest` is null, still show these rows and their links: they are a comparison, not a verification. Do not call them confirmed, and do not name a verified cheapest.

affiliate.description: False when this link earns WEM nothing: the shop has no affiliate programme with WEM, or this link does not carry one. It is still a real offer, and its link is not affiliate-tracked. Absent (or true) means the link is affiliate-tracked. `disclosure` states whether all, some or none of the links are tracked.

inStock.description: null means the retailer did not report availability. Say "stock not confirmed" — never present null as in stock.

totalCost.description: Item plus any stated extras. When unknown is non-empty, delivered is a floor — never relay it as what the shopper will pay.

receipt.description: Citation handle for this answer. Field names follow ACP suggested_price (observed_at, source, amount). signed is true only when WEM issued an HMAC with a dedicated key; otherwise false (fail closed).

amount.description: Major-unit decimal, same units as verify_offer prices.

amount_minor.description: Integer minor units of amount, ACP form.

issuedAt.description: Alias of observed_at, kept for the unsigned edition.

observed_at.description: When WEM read the price in amount, or "unobserved" when nothing dates it — then do not present amount as current. ACP #197.

signed.description: True when WEM signed this receipt with a dedicated HMAC key. False when no key is configured (fail closed). Never derived from CRON_SECRET.

source.description: Citable URI of the standard this receipt is issued under.

sameModel.description: Present only when the maker's own page says another model code is this product and a person at WEM has checked it. These are NOT offers for the product asked about: they are not part of `offers`, and none is this product's lowest price or the best deal. On verify_offer they are not part of the check: `verdict`, `cheapest`, `betterBy`, `summary` and the receipt are about the product asked about, and a cheaper sister code never makes the claimed price wrong. `summary` is written to be quoted as it is. `maker.host` is the source of the claim. `url` is WEM's comparison for that model, not a shop. When `relation` is `differs`, the `differences` are what the maker says differs, and its price is not a saving. Absent is not evidence that no equivalent exists.

cheapest.description: The other model's cheapest named shop. Null when no named shop has an in-stock price for it. `priceAgeDays` gives its age; without one it is not current.

priceAgeDays.description: Days since WEM read that price. Null means undated.

checkedOn.description: When a person at WEM read the maker’s page (YYYY-MM-DD).

differences.description: What the maker says differs. Empty when identical.

maker.description: The maker's own page that says so: the proof. WEM is not the source of the claim.

model.description: The other model code, as the maker writes it.

relation.description: `identical`: the maker says it is the same product. `differs`: the same product except `differences`; not like for like.

summary.description: WEM’s words for it, written to be quoted as they are.

url.description: WEM's comparison for that model, not a shop.

summary.description: Written so quoting it verbatim is accurate. Prefer quoting it to paraphrasing the verdict code.
